Drew Brees. An American quarterback recognized as one of the most accurate and prolific passers in NFL history. Signed by the New Orleans Saints in 2006 after the team's relocation following Hurricane Katrina, he led the franchise to a Super Bowl championship and became synonymous with the team's return to prominence. Drafted second round by the San Diego Chargers in 2001, he spent his first five seasons there before signing with New Orleans. He won the Super Bowl XLIV championship after the 2009 season with the Saints, leading the team to its first championship in franchise history just four years after relocating from San Diego. He threw for eighty thousand three hundred fifty-seven career passing yards and five hundred seventy-one touchdowns, both among the all-time NFL leaders and becoming the first quarterback to eclipse eighty thousand yards. He earned thirteen Pro Bowl selections and won one NFL MVP award in 2008, establishing himself as a model of consistency and durability. Renowned for his accuracy and decision-making, he led multiple playoff runs and defined an era of Saints football throughout the 2000s and 2010s. He played fifteen seasons with the Saints, unusual among modern Hall-of-Fame-caliber quarterbacks, remaining through age 41 before finishing his career with one season elsewhere.
